finding.claim: Address6.parse() bad-character branch puts raw input into AddressError.parseMessage without HTML escaping, contrary to the documented contract that parseMessage is HTML-escaped and safe to insert as-is.
finding.source: Any string passed to the Address6 constructor (ipv6.ts:113, parse call at ipv6.ts:157), e.g. an address-inspector UI text field.
finding.sink: parseMessage built by address.replace(RE_BAD_CHARACTERS, '$1') at src/ipv6.ts:808 (also 817 for the bad-address branch, which is safe because only hex/colon reach it).

trace.note: raw address with non-hex chars wrapped in span but otherwise unescaped goes into parseMessage
doc claims parseMessage is HTML-escaped and safe to insert as-is
sibling path escapes prefix via helpers.escapeHtml before building error HTML; bad-character branch does not
RE_BAD_CHARACTERS = /([^0-9a-f:/%])/gi wraps but does not encode

finding.guards_checked: Address6 constructor subnet and zone stripping (ipv6.ts:122-153) rejects '/' but does not encode. parse4in6 (ipv6.ts:741-788) escapes only its own prefix. AddressError constructor (address-error.ts:15-21) does no encoding. Text-context exploitation is not possible: every raw '<' is immediately followed by the library's '', so no tag can form. Attribute-context exploitation is unverified (no working payload constructed). Severity low; PLAUSIBLE.
